nameStory: The "freckled" in Freckled Tube Lichen comes from the scattered spots and markings that often dot its surface, giving it a speckled appearance like freckles on skin. The "tube" part refers to the hollow, tube-like lobes that are characteristic of all lichens in the Hypogymnia genus - if you gently break open a lobe, you'll find it's hollow inside like a tiny green straw.
description: Freckled Tube Lichen is a leafy (foliose) lichen that grows in overlapping, branched lobes on tree bark and rocks. The lobes are typically gray-green to brownish-green and have a distinctive hollow, tube-like structure when you examine them closely. This medium-sized lichen forms patches that can spread several inches across, with individual lobes reaching about half an inch wide. Like other tube lichens, it has a distinctive inflated appearance that sets it apart from flatter, more typical leafy lichens.

idTips.label: Growth Form
idTips.description: Hollow, tube-like lobes that feel slightly puffy and inflated when gently pressed - break one open and you'll see it's actually hollow inside like a tiny tunnel

idTips.label: Color
idTips.description: Gray-green to brownish-green when dry, becoming more vibrant green when wet from rain or morning dew

idTips.label: Surface Texture
idTips.description: Scattered dark spots or "freckles" on the upper surface, with a smooth to slightly wrinkled texture that feels papery-thin

idTips.label: Substrate
idTips.description: Grows on bark of both deciduous and coniferous trees, occasionally on rocks, usually attached at the center with lobes spreading outward

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Forms patches 2-4 inches across with individual lobes about 1/4 to 1/2 inch wide and slightly shorter in length

habitat: Look for Freckled Tube Lichen on the bark of trees in mixed and coniferous forests throughout New England's mountains and hills. It particularly favors slightly acidic bark and can be found on both hardwoods like maples and oaks, as well as conifers like spruce and fir. You'll often spot it in areas with good air quality, as it's sensitive to pollution.

seasonality.spring: More vibrant green coloration as spring rains moisten the lichen, making the freckled patterns more visible and the texture slightly softer to touch.
seasonality.summer: Appears more grayish and dried out during hot, dry periods, with lobes feeling crispier and more brittle, but still maintains its distinctive hollow structure.
seasonality.fall: Color shifts back toward gray-green as humidity increases, and the lichen becomes more pliable again as autumn moisture returns.
seasonality.winter: Remains visible on tree bark but appears quite gray and dormant, though the tube-like structure is still apparent and useful for identification even when snow-covered.

funFact: If you gently squeeze a lobe of Freckled Tube Lichen between your fingers, you're actually compressing a living air conditioning system - the hollow tubes help regulate moisture and gas exchange, essentially allowing the lichen to "breathe" through its inflated structure!
confusionNotes: Most easily confused with other tube lichens in the same genus, but the scattered dark freckles on the surface are your best clue. Remember: "Freckled has freckles" - those dark spots are much more prominent than on its smooth-surfaced relatives.
compareHints: Freckled Tube Lichen differs from Hooded Tube Lichen by having scattered dark spots rather than smooth surfaces, and from Powder-headed Tube Lichen by lacking the powdery white soredia (reproductive dust) at the lobe tips. Unlike Lattice Tube Lichen, which has a more intricate, net-like branching pattern, Freckled Tube Lichen has simpler, less divided lobes with its characteristic speckled appearance.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Unlike its tube lichen relatives, Hooded Tube Lichen has those distinctive pepper-like black dots scattered across its surface and more pronounced upward-curling edges.
Among the tube lichens in New England, Powder-headed Tube Lichen has the most inflated, balloon-like lobes compared to its relatives.
Unlike its relative the Hooded Tube Lichen which has more inflated, hood-like lobes, Lattice Tube Lichen has distinctly hollow, narrower tubes.
